clue.text: They tell tales of referees

definitions.meaning: first meaning: people who expose wrongdoing to the authorities
second meaning, taken literally: match officials who blow whistles

explanation.surface: Somebody gossips about the officials at a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is literal: referees are the people who blow the whistle in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Informants who expose wrongdoing are called by this name, and match officials literally sound a whistle to stop play.

clue.text: News flash! Cut out the vigilance!

indicators.note: 'out' can mean wrong or not in place, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An editor shouts a breaking bulletin and orders that the alertness be cut from the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut out' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'Cut' is fodder and 'out' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns describe the state of being alert and keeping a careful eye open for danger.

clue.text: Drive another mile, parking in the centre

indicators.note: something placed in the centre goes inside the other letters
'another' version of a word is a different arrangement of its letters

parts.note: the letters of mile rearranged
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A motorist drives one more mile, looking for a parking spot in the town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like part of the motoring story but is the definition, used in the sense of forcing onwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To force or urge someone forward is to drive them, the verb sense of pushing into action.

clue.text: Sleaze which sticks?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tacky as in cheap and tasteless

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the quality of stickiness
definitions.meaning: second meaning: tacky as in slightly sticky, like drying paint

explanation.surface: A wry question about whether scandal clings to a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Tacky has two senses: cheap and vulgar, and slightly sticky. The noun covers both.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheap vulgarity is tackiness in one sense, and the gluey quality of half-dry glue is tackiness in another.

clue.text: Welshman getting a leg up — that's good news

parts.note: Evan is a typical Welsh first name

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word sent up is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written; the a is padding

explanation.surface: A Welshman is given a leg up, a helpful boost, which is welcome news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A leg up' looks like the idiom for help, but in this down clue the leg is written upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Evangel is an old word for the gospel, which literally means glad tidings or joyful message.

clue.text: Upholder of the bible

parts.note: surface reading: a staunch defender of scripture and its teachings
setter's reading: something that physically holds the book up in church

explanation.surface: A devout believer who defends scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: Upholder suggests a person defending the faith; it is literally a stand that holds the book up.
explanation.definitionFit: A reading stand in a church supports the large Bible from which lessons are read aloud.

clue.text: Savage sounding writer

indicators.note: 'sounding' tells us to go by how the word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: savage means untamed, a word pronounced the same as the surname

explanation.surface: A critic describes an author with a ferocious reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar Wilde was the Irish playwright and wit.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde wrote plays, poems and a novel, so he is a well-known example of an author.

clue.text: No longer needed and turned out

definitions.note: past participle, as in made jobless
definitions.meaning: second meaning: dismissed from a job when the post is cut

explanation.surface: Something surplus gets thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a worker made redundant has lost their job because the role is no longer required.
explanation.definitionFit: Superfluous things are unnecessary, and British employees laid off because their jobs vanished are described the same way.

clue.text: Photo? Picture? Some subject!

indicators.note: 'some' of the words means only part of them, a run of letters inside

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: An exasperated exclamation about what an image is meant to depict.
explanation.definitionFit: The subject of a discussion or essay is the theme it deals with, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Tap on the shoulder

parts.note: surface reading: a light touch to catch someone's attention
setter's reading: the sword touching each shoulder when a knighthood is conferred

explanation.walkthrough: The touch of the sword on the shoulder in knighting is the original meaning; it now means any honour or praise.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial sword touch bestowing knighthood gave its name to any award or mark of honour.

clue.text: Main way to carry blood around?

definitions.text: Main way to carry blood around

parts.words: Main way to carry blood around
parts.note: surface reading: the body's chief vessel circulating blood
setter's reading: a principal route for traffic, named after the blood vessels

explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like anatomy; the answer is a major highway, so named because it acts like an artery.
explanation.definitionFit: A major highway carrying through traffic is named by analogy with the large vessels pumping blood from the heart.

clue.text: Serving a portion of food

definitions.meaning: first meaning: assisting, as a present participle
second meaning: a plateful dished up

explanation.surface: A waiter dishes up a plate at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving' reads as a noun matching the second half, but here it is the verb sense of assisting.
explanation.definitionFit: Aiding someone is lending a hand, and a plateful dished out at a meal is also a second or seconds.

clue.text: Girl, one with real potential

indicators.note: potential is what something could become, so the letters may become a new word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A talent scout spots a young woman with genuine promise.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleanor is a female first name, and girl in crosswords often stands for any woman's name.

clue.text: Pawnbroker's dirty article gone missing

indicators.note: something gone missing has been taken away from the word

parts.note: dirty means not clean
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A pawnbroker's soiled item has disappeared from the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker; pawned goods were said to be at my uncle's.
explanation.definitionFit: In dated British slang a pawnbroker was nicknamed the family relative, so goods in hock were with him.

clue.text: Moscow organisation once found using non-metric conversion

indicators.note: a conversion changes something into another form, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A Soviet body is discovered converting units away from the metric system.
explanation.walkthrough: The Comintern was the Communist International, run from Moscow from 1919 until 1943.
explanation.definitionFit: The Communist International was a body directed from the Soviet capital that was dissolved during the Second World War.

clue.text: Comes down on headland painting

parts.note: an aircraft that comes down lands
a cape is a headland jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Something descends onto a promontory, perhaps a bird or plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painting' is a noun here: a picture of countryside or scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture showing natural scenery such as fields, hills or coast is a genre of art in its own right.

clue.text: Mocking its racial trouble?

indicators.note: trouble suggests disturbance, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about whether a piece deriding racial strife is itself offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Satire ridicules its targets, so writing that derides or lampoons is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Means changing wine inside for those sharing a title

indicators.note: inside tells us one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the letters of means rearranged

indicators.note: changing the word means rearranging its letters

parts.note: sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Methods of swapping in a different wine, as a sommelier might plan.
explanation.definitionFit: People or things bearing the same name as each other are described by this noun, with title meaning name.

clue.text: Shoot up the joint

parts.note: surface reading: gangsters spraying bullets around a bar or club
setter's reading: the knee, a body joint, as the target of a paramilitary punishment shot

explanation.walkthrough: Joint is slang for a seedy venue, but here it is the knee; the verb means to shoot someone through the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramilitary punishment shootings aimed at the knee are known by this verb, firing a bullet into that body joint.

clue.text: Second summons to work on shellfish

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a summons is a call to attend
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A second call-out to come and work on a seafood catch.
explanation.definitionFit: This bivalve mollusc with a fan-shaped ribbed shell is eaten as seafood, a direct example of a shellfish.

clue.text: An instruction to all on the staff

definitions.text: An instruction to all on the staff

parts.words: An instruction to all on the staff
parts.note: surface reading: a memo to every employee
setter's reading: the five-line stave of written music, carrying a direction for every player

explanation.walkthrough: Staff here is the musical stave. The answer is Italian for all, telling the whole orchestra to play together.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed on a score, this Italian direction tells every performer to play together, as opposed to a soloist alone.

clue.text: Honest! It's wrong for the Queen to be in the established church

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside

parts.note: CE is the Church of England, England's established church
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A protest that the monarch should not belong to the state church.
explanation.walkthrough: The British monarch is in fact head of the Church of England, which gives the surface its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone honest means what they say, which is exactly what genuine and heartfelt describe.

clue.text: Beer has no head? That is very weird

indicators.note: without a head means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: taken as written
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is

explanation.surface: A drinker is spooked by a pint with no froth on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like the froth on a pint, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something strange and unsettling in a spooky way is uncanny, the sense of the adjective here.

clue.text: Spray a rose, perhaps, with oil one left out

indicators.note: perhaps hints the words are only a possible form, to be rearranged
something left out is removed from the word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Instructions to mist a rose bush, maybe adding oil but leaving one out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spray a rose' reads as a gardening task; 'Spray' alone is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A pressurised can that releases a fine mist is a spray, and the word covers both container and mist.

clue.text: He set about making rope for sailors

indicators.note: setting things about scatters them in various directions, rearranging the letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man goes about making rope for a ship's crew.
explanation.walkthrough: On a boat a sheet is not a sail but the line used to trim a sail.
explanation.definitionFit: In nautical language the line controlling the angle of a sail carries this name, which landlubbers would expect to be cloth.

clue.text: Many fancy recital with a regular beat …

indicators.note: fancy as a verb hints at imaginative reworking, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: M, a thousand in Roman numerals, stands for many
the letters of recital rearranged

explanation.surface: Many an elaborate musical performance has a steady rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse or music in a measured, regular rhythm is described with the adjective formed from metre.

clue.text: … which I believe is a sacred orchestral piece

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Latin for these words
second meaning: the section of a musical Mass setting the creed

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a believer describes a church concert work.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the previous clue's music for the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for the opening of the creed, this word also names the movement of a sung Mass that sets that statement of faith.

clue.text: Not having enough people to tour Nepal, duped organisation

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tour company that cheated customers going to Nepal could not fill its group.
explanation.definitionFit: A place with too few inhabitants for its size or resources is described with this adjective about sparse populations.
